acceptanceCriteria: A context packet for a subject reserves every tracked AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md) on the path from the repository root to the subject's directory, closest first, each with its own evidence row.
A fixture with root and nested AGENTS.md proves the nested file is cited and ranked ahead of the root file for a subject under it.
TCP-V0-008 is amended in the same change and REQUIREMENTS.tsv regenerated.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Observed: `corvint context --task ... --subject apps/fetfinder/components/WorkspaceProfileCardHeader.tsx` on the MeVille clone (Corvint 0.8.1 build 82) cited only the root `AGENTS.md` as governing; `apps/fetfinder/components/AGENTS.md`, the scope document in the subject's own directory, was absent from all results. Cause: `internal/contextindex/taskcontext.go:1212` fixes the precedence to root-level names and states that no other nested instruction path is eligible. The AGENTS.md convention (agents.md) says the closest file takes precedence, and Codex and Claude Code both load nested files. This contradicts invariant 3 (project-owned authority first) on any repository that scopes instructions per directory, and it will surface in V1-0019 untouched-repository validation.
title: context: a nested AGENTS.md in the subject's own directory is not admitted as governing evidence
